base.description: The switch as the base AC order ships: one Routing Engine (RE0), three AC power supplies, four fan trays and the blank panels, with both line card slots covered. Line cards are ordered separately.

base-ac.description: EX9253-BASE-AC: the EX9253-CHAS-3RU chassis with one Routing Engine (EX9253-RE), four fan trays (JNP-FAN-3RU), three AC power supplies (JNP-PWR1600-AC, in PSM0 to PSM2 as drawn), the cable management bracket and air filter unit (JNP-CM-3RU) and blank panels for the empty slots (EX9253-LC-BLNK). First Junos OS release 18.2R1. Front-to-back airflow.

base-dc.description: EX9253-BASE-DC: as the base AC order with three DC power supplies (JNP-PWR1100-DC) in place of the AC ones.

chas.description: EX9253-CHAS-3RU, the spare chassis (datasheet FRU table). It ships without Routing Engines, supplies or fan trays, which are ordered separately; the bays are shown open.

red-ac.description: EX9253-RED-AC: the redundant order, with two Routing Engines (RE0 and RE1) and four AC power supplies (PSM0 to PSM3 as drawn); otherwise as the base AC order.

red-dc.description: EX9253-RED-DC: the redundant order with two Routing Engines and four DC power supplies (JNP-PWR1100-DC).

datasheet.title: Juniper EX9250 Ethernet Switch Datasheet (1000632-006-EN, Sep 2021)

description: Juniper EX9253, a 3RU modular core and aggregation switch that runs Junos OS, the larger of the two EX9250 chassis. The front has two Routing Engine slots (RE0 and RE1) across the top and two line card slots (MPC1 above MPC0) below, with the ESD point between the Routing Engines. The rear has six power supply slots (PSM0 to PSM5), three each side, and four fan trays between them (FT0 to FT3). The base order ships one Routing Engine, three supplies and the blank panels; the redundant order two Routing Engines and four supplies. Line cards are ordered separately and are not modelled here: both line card slots show their blank panels.

gaps.note: Width: 19 in (48.26 cm) in the guide's Table 5 and the datasheet, which is with the brackets, and 17.4 in (44.2 cm) in the specifications page, which the figure's fold lines match. Height: 5.21 in (132.3 mm) in the guide, 5.217 in in the datasheet and 5.25 in (133.4 mm) in the specifications page. Depth: 30 in (762 mm) in all three, with 36.5 or 38.5 in in the guide when the brackets and handles are counted. The specifications page's width and the guide's height and depth are carried.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis, or Juniper's confirmation of the body width and height
The part numbers of the front-mounting and rear-mounting brackets and of the cable management bracket, which the guide lists by name only, and the bracket extents.

The cable management bracket and the air filter unit (JNP-CM-3RU, Figures 5 and 10). They bolt onto the front of the chassis in front of the line cards and are drawn in no flat figure; the guide's Table 5 gives the pair as 19 in wide, 5.43 in deep and 5.19 in high. They are not drawn.

The EX9253-6Q12C and EX9253-6Q12C-M line cards (Tables 14 and 18, Figures 18 and 19), each with six QSFP+ and twelve QSFP28 ports and a lamp block, and the EX9253-BND1 bundle that pairs a base chassis with a 6Q12C card. The guide's base and redundant orders ship no card, so the two bays show blank panels. A line card family is a separate piece of work.

gaps.note: Table 5 gives the supplies 1.63 in (41.4 mm) high; the rear figures stack three on a 40.3 mm pitch, 39 to 40 mm high. The bays carry the figure's 39.6 mm, the table's width of 86.7 mm.
gaps.wanted: Juniper's confirmation of the supply face height
which power supply slots the base and the redundant orders populate
The protective earthing terminal, a two-hole terminal on the side of the chassis (Figure 28); the guide draws it in an isometric figure with no scale, so the side faces are left empty.

The slot legends RE0, MPC1, MPC0, RE1 and PSM0 to PSM5 printed on the ears and the fan tray legends FT0 to FT3 on the lower lip. The ears are not drawn; the PSM legends that sit on the body are drawn.
The colour of the fan tray handle. The guide draws the tray as a line drawing and states no colour or airflow code; the tray is drawn dark grey with the label AIR OUT.
What the BITS jack carries on the Routing Engine, a T1, an E1 or another clock signal. The guide gives no rate or framing.
A straight-on photograph of the front and of the rear; every position comes from the guide's flat figures.
The Junos names of the line card ports. The guide's Table 4 names FPC and PIC slots 0 and 1 and refers to the Hardware Compatibility Tool for transceivers.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the divider between the Routing Engines (guide Figure 4)

fans.description: Four fan trays, FT0 to FT3 from the left, each with two counter-rotating fans. The guide says a fully configured switch needs all four to operate normally and a failed tray must be replaced at once; it states no N+M form

lc-slots.description: The two line card slots, MPC0 at the bottom and MPC1 above it (guide Figure 1, callout 2)

attrs.redundancy-note: Datasheet, Table 1: the EX9253 "holds up to six power supplies" with "-40 to -72 V DC (3+1 redundancy)" and the same for 100-120 V AC and 200-240 V AC. Six slots, PSM0 to PSM5; a base order ships three supplies and a redundant order four. Do not mix AC and DC supplies

Guide, Host Subsystem in an EX9253 Switch: "If two REs are installed, one functions as the primary and the other functions as the backup." A base order has one Routing Engine and a redundant order two

re-slots.description: The two Routing Engine slots across the top of the front, RE0 and RE1 from the left (guide Figure 1, callout 1)

name: ex9253

airflow.note: The guide: the switch has front-to-back (AIR OUT) airflow, intake at the front of the chassis, including for the power supplies, and exhaust at the rear. There is no back-to-front build, so no airflow configuration is written.

chassis.note: Guide Table 5: 5.21 in (13.23 cm, 3 U) high; 19 in (48.26 cm) wide; 30 in (76.2 cm) deep without the cable management brackets, air filter unit and handles, or 36.5 in (92.7 cm) with them on an AC chassis and 38.5 in (97.79 cm) on a DC one; 50 lb (22.68 kg) without a FRU, 157.4 lb (71.4 kg) AC and 163.4 lb (74.11 kg) DC fully loaded. The datasheet gives 19 x 5.217 x 30 in and the specifications page 17.4 x 5.25 x 30 in (44.2 x 13.3 x 76.2 cm). The 19 in is the width with the front-mounting brackets, so the body is the specifications page's 44.2 cm, which the figure agrees with: its fold lines are 75 and 1413 px apart at 3.03 px/mm, 442.0 mm. The height is the guide's 132.3 mm. See the gap named chassis-size.

colour.note: No photograph of the EX9253 is held. The chassis is drawn the grey of the EX9251's photograph, #8b8e94, a relative and not a reading of this chassis; Figures 1 and 2 are line drawings.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide mounts the switch on four posts of a 19 in rack or cabinet with front-mounting brackets and rear-mounting brackets that slide on the chassis sides (Figures 23 to 27), and has a cable management bracket (Figure 5). No rail or mounting kit has a part number, and the library holds no contract for the brackets, so chassis.ears and chassis.kits are left out and a gap says so.

esd.note: Figure 4 shows the ESD point on the front panel (a hex-nut jack with the ESD mark under it), and Figure 1 places it on the divider between the Routing Engines, 218.9 mm across and 11.1 mm down, with the mark at 29.9 mm.

gate-1.note: Guide Figures 1 and 2 are 1500 px wide rasters of the front and the AC rear, drawn flat. The outline, ears included, is 1461 x 400 px, an aspect of 3.65 against 482.6 / 132.3 = 3.65 (0.1 percent out), so both are read as flat at 3.03 px/mm. The body is the metal between the fold lines at 75 and 1413 px, 442.0 mm; the ears outside them carry the slot legends (RE0, MPC1, MPC0 and RE1, MPC1, MPC0) and are not drawn. Rows are taken from the top outline at 149.5 px (front) and 144.5 px (rear). Every position read off these figures is estimated to about 0.7 mm: a pixel is 0.33 mm.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice. No Juniper bulletin was found. Two third-party trackers (endoflife.ai, parkplacetechnologies.com) give an end of service life of 2027-03-31 for the EX9253-BASE-AC, with no last order date; that is not a Juniper notice, so none is written as announced.

modules.note: The Routing Engines, supplies and fan trays are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. The line cards (EX9253-6Q12C and EX9253-6Q12C-M, Tables 14 and 18) are named but not modelled: the guide says they are not part of the base or the redundant order ("you must order them separately"), so each line card bay accepts the blank panel only and ships with it. The air filter unit and the cable management bracket (JNP-CM-3RU) bolt onto the front of the chassis and are not drawn (see the gap named cable-management). The slot-by-slot cooling note: the blank panel for a line card slot is EX9253-LC-BLNK, for a Routing Engine slot EX9253-RE-BLNK (datasheet FRU table only), and the guide names no part number for a supply or a fan tray panel.

power.note: Guide Tables 9 and 11: AC system input 2500 W at 25 A (low line 90 to 140 VAC, high line 180 to 264 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz); DC system input 2500 W at 54 A at -48 VDC (operating -40 to -72 VDC). Table 13: line cards 740 W typical and 800 W maximum (EX9253-6Q12C) or 770 and 835 W (the -M card, which the datasheet's Table 2 gives as 770 and 770), the Routing Engine 58 and 65 W, a fan tray 20 and 95 W, at 25 C and 55 C. The datasheet's Table 3 gives a maximum power draw of 2692 W for both AC and DC. They are different scopes and the figures are kept as printed.

psu-population.note: The guide says a base order ships three supplies and a redundant order four, and the figures show all six slots filled, but no document says which slots the shipped supplies take. They are placed in PSM0, PSM1 and PSM2 (and PSM3), and the other slots show the blank panel the guide says ships for each empty slot. The guide says "in a base configuration, if one power supply fails or is removed, one of the line cards is disabled".

rear-layout.note: Figures 2 and 3 at 3.03 px/mm: three power supply slots in a column at each side, PSM0, PSM2 and PSM4 at the left and PSM1, PSM3 and PSM5 at the right (Figure 2's rotated legends), each 87 mm wide on a 40.5 mm pitch; and four fan trays between them, FT0 to FT3 from the left, 62.0 mm wide on a 62.3 mm pitch and 125.5 mm high. The fan tray legends FT0 to FT3 are printed on the lower lip below each tray and are not drawn. The guide's CLI table numbers the supplies PEM0 to PEM3 and the redundancy section PEM0 to PEM5 (and the power section PSM0 to PSM5); the printed legend is PSM and is followed.

slots.note: Figure 1 at 3.03 px/mm: the two Routing Engine openings are 569 px, 188 mm wide and start at 24.1 and 226.3 mm; the two line card openings are 417 mm wide and start at 9.9 mm, MPC1 at 46.4 mm down and MPC0 at 89.2 mm, each 41.9 mm high (Table 5's line card is 16.5 x 1.65 in, 419.1 x 41.9 mm). Callout 1 is the host subsystem and callout 2 the line cards. The slot labels are MPC0 and MPC1 (the guide says "line card slots labeled MPC0 and MPC1" and numbers them from the bottom) and RE0 and RE1 from the left.

sources.note: Juniper EX9253 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2022-11-30, 251 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2022), https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex9253/ex9253.pdf: Tables 1 to 4 (the line cards, power supplies, orders and CLI names), the front and rear views (Figures 1 to 4), the host subsystem (Figures 6 and 7, Table 6), the cooling system (Figures 8 to 12, Table 7), the power system (Figures 13 to 17, Tables 8 to 13), the chassis (Table 5), the line cards (Tables 14 and 18), the environmental table (Table 23) and the parts lists (Tables 32 and 33). EX9250 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000632-006-EN, Sep 2021 (PDF produced 2022-07-27): the chassis table (Table 5), the power tables and the ordering table. The datasheet's own address now redirects to a page on the hpe.com site, which did not answer; the PDF was read from the Internet Archive's capture of Juniper's address (https://web.archive.org/web/20240111201612/https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex9250-ethernet-switch-datasheet.pdf). Juniper's EX9250 specifications page (https://www.juniper.net/us/en/products/switches/ex-series/ex9250-core-and-aggregation-switches/specs.html) for the body width. Terms: the documents are Juniper's, read here for facts only, and nothing of them is copied into the library. No photograph of the EX9253 was reachable: Juniper's image library holds one image of the EX9250 line (ex9250-11) and it shows the EX9251. No held intake folder, Visio stencil or 3D model was reachable from this work, so the public documents above are the only sources.
